title: AMECEA: Ahead of July Plenary, AMECEA Executive Board Meets to Reflect on Four-Year Mandate
desc:
Sr. Jecinter Antoinette Okoth, FSSA
The Executive Board of the Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa (AMECEA) convened for a two-day meeting at Donum Dei in Nairobi, Kenya, with the board's chairman calling members to reflect on whether they have fulfilled the mandate entrusted to them by the 2022 Plenary Assembly.
Opening the meeting, AMECEA Chairman and Bishop of the Diocese of Solwezi in Zambia, Bishop Charles Sampa Kasonde, said, This is a journey we started four years ago in Tanzania after the 20th Plenary Assembly in 2022. The plenary entrusted us with this opportunity to be the midwives between the plenaries.
The Executive Board was mandated in October 2022 to oversee the implementation of regional priorities identified during the Plenary Assembly, primarily by communicating those priorities to member conferences and ensuring that conferences deliberated on them and generated concrete resolutions.
In their first Executive Board meeting, which took place from 18- 19 October, 2022, after the Plenary Assembly that was held in Tanzania, the Chairman called on the new AMECEA Board members to embrace the responsibility they were given with Commitment and zeal.
“Let us take up our responsibility with commitment and zeal to fulfill our mandate and ensure the pastoral relevance of our member episcopal conferences is actively presented,” Bishop Kasonde told the new board members then and added, “We shall deliberate on matters pertaining to the running of the AMECEA family of God comprising all the nations in the region, and we shall be guided by the statutes and the constitution of the Church in the way of running our region and of the plenary from one plenary to the next that is from July 2022-July 2026.”
As the board now approaches the end of its term, Bishop Kasonde, on Thursday, May 7, challenged members to critically assess the quality of their stewardship.
We need to judge ourselves on how we have executed the mandate we were given. Have we stood worthy of our call? he posed to the delegates.
With the upcoming 21st AMECEA Plenary Assembly scheduled for 18th to 26th July this year, the Zambian Bishop underscored the urgency of self-evaluation. Are we saying we have done justice to the work we were given by the plenary? Are we saying we have achieved the goals, and are we happy as we go to the next plenary in July? What is it that we are going to showcase before the plenary? he posed.
Drawing on the famous dictum by the ancient Greek philosopher Socrates, as recorded by philosopher Plato, Bishop Kasonde grounded his call to reflection in a deeper wisdom. The unexamined life is not worth living’; here we are, time for us to reflect, he said.
The chairman expressed appreciation for the work of the AMECEA Secretariat and delegates from member conferences, noting that attendance at meetings and feedback from conferences have been encouraging throughout the term.
He further reminded the board members of the historic significance of the meeting, saying, Let us embrace this time as the last moment of our board meeting, as the next will be for preparation of the plenary.
